chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Abdul Azeem ibn Abdullah al-Hassani (may God be pleased with him), on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus, on the authority of Yunus ibn Zabyan that Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

For Fatimah, near the Honorable, the Exalted God, there are nine names: Fatimah, As-Siddiqah, Al-Mubarakah, At-Tahirah, Az-Zakiyah, Ar-Radiyah, Al-Mardiyyah, Al-Muhadathah, and Az-Zahra. Then he (peace be upon him) said: Do you understand the interpretation of the name Fatimah? I said: Inform me, my Master. He said: She has been purified from evil. He said: Then he said: Had not the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) married her, no one else on the face of the earth other than Adam and those below him would have been found to match her until the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What are the nine names of Fatimah (as) and what does the name 'Fatimah' signify?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to establish Fatimah al-Zahra’s unique ontological status, where the etymology of 'Fatimah' as 'severed from evil' underscores her innate purity (Ismah). The Imam’s declaration that no one from Adam to the end of time was her equal (Kufu) except Ali highlights the theological principle of marital compatibility based on spiritual rank, a cornerstone of Shia genealogy and Imamate legitimacy.
